sections.h2: Where is the Vilas County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Vilas County Register of Deeds is in the Vilas County Courthouse at 330 Court Street in Eagle River, and the phone number is 715.479.3660. The office is open 8am to 4pm Monday through Friday and closes on holidays.

Paper documents must arrive by the 3:00pm recording cutoff. Electronic submissions have an earlier cutoff of 2:45pm. The county office page says the counter takes only cash or check, so plan payment before you drive to Eagle River. Staff cannot draft documents or give legal advice, which means your deed should come from a title company, closing agent or attorney.

sections.h2: What does the Register of Deeds record when a Vilas County house sells?
sections.html:
The office records deeds, land contracts, mortgages and real property financing statements, and it keeps birth, death and marriage records in the same building. Under Wis. Stat. 59.43(1c), the register stamps each recorded document with the date, hour and minute, numbers it in sequence and indexes it for the public.

That time stamp matters in a sale. Under Wis. Stat. 706.08(1)(a), a conveyance that is not recorded is void against a later buyer who acts in good faith, pays value and records first. A deed that sits in a drawer leaves the new owner exposed.

The county posts several forms that Vilas County sellers and heirs run into:

  • Standard Form and Document Requirements, which describe how a document must look before it is accepted
  • Termination of Decedent's Property Interest, with its own instruction sheet
  • Designation of TOD Beneficiary
  • Registration of Firm Name, with an instruction sheet

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Vilas County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed costs $30 under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag), and the seller also owes the state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value. Copies cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page, plus $1 to certify.

ItemAmount or ruleSource
Recording any document$30Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag)
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added page, $1 more to certifyWis. Stat. 59.43(2)(b)
Real estate transfer fee$0.30 per $100 of value or fraction, paid by the grantorWis. Stat. 77.22(1)
Paper recording cutoff3:00pmVilas County Register of Deeds
E-recording cutoff2:45pmVilas County Register of Deeds

A $200,000 sale produces a transfer fee of $600, which is $200,000 divided by $100 and multiplied by $0.30. The register collects the fee when the deed is submitted. Under Wis. Stat. 77.24, the county keeps 20 percent and sends the rest to the state.

sections.h2: What is the real estate transfer return and who files it?
sections.html:
The real estate transfer return, called the RETR, is the electronic form that accompanies a deed, and the Wisconsin Department of Revenue runs it through My Tax Account. The grantor and grantee both sign, and the register cannot accept a conveyance for recording without a completed return unless the transfer is exempt.

The Department of Revenue overview lists what you need before you start:

  • The completed deed
  • Names, addresses, phone numbers and emails for each grantor and grantee
  • Social Security, ITIN or FEIN numbers for the parties
  • Parcel numbers from the property tax bill

After you submit, print the receipt and take it to the Register of Deeds with the notarized deed and payment. The Vilas County page also warns that the state updated its RETR system, so check the state site for current screens. Underreporting value by 25 percent or more, or claiming an exemption that does not apply, brings a penalty of $25 or 25 percent of the extra fee, whichever is greater.

sections.h2: Which Vilas County transfers skip the transfer fee?
sections.html:
Many family and estate transfers are exempt from the fee, though they may still need a return. The list in Wis. Stat. 77.25 and the state's exemption guide includes these:

  • Transfers by will, descent or survivorship
  • Transfers between spouses
  • Transfers between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration
  • A foreclosure deed or deed in lieu of foreclosure to a mortgage holder or land contract seller
  • A transfer on death under Wis. Stat. 705.15, and the designation of a TOD beneficiary
  • Real estate worth $1,000 or less

The reason for any exemption must be stated on the face of the deed by subsection number. The Department of Revenue states that if the exemption you expected does not appear in the dropdown for your document and parties, the conveyance is subject to the fee. The register does not judge the value or the exemption, so the signers carry that responsibility.

sections.h2: Can I record a Vilas County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. Vilas County accepts e-recording through three vendors: Simplifile at 800-460-5657, CSC eRecording Solutions at 866-652-0111, and Hopdox at 385-501-5103. Your title company or closing agent normally handles the upload, and the cutoff for these submissions is 2:45pm.

Paper documents still need to meet the format rules in Wis. Stat. 59.43(2m). The register may refuse a document that does not substantially comply, so ask your preparer to check these points:

  • A 3 inch by 3 inch blank space in the upper right corner of the first page
  • Page size of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches
  • Black, blue or red ink and margins of at least a quarter inch
  • Parcel identification number, clear names for grantor and grantee, and the drafter's name

The county also lists a Land Notification Alerts sign-up on its Register of Deeds page, with text alerts available.

sections.h2: What should Vilas County owners know before selling?
sections.html:
Vilas County covers 1,018 square miles in the north of the state, and 161 of those square miles are water. The county counts 1,318 lakes, and much of the land lies inside the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest and the Northern Highland-American Legion State Forest. Eagle River is the county seat and the only city. The towns include Arbor Vitae, Boulder Junction, Conover, Lac du Flambeau, Land O' Lakes, Manitowish Waters, Phelps, St. Germain and Winchester. The reservation of the Lac du Flambeau Band of Lake Superior Chippewa overlaps part of the county.

The 2020 census recorded 23,047 residents and 24,486 housing units, and 55.9 percent of those units were vacant. That high share fits a recreation county where many homes are second homes and cabins. Of the occupied homes, 81.1 percent were owner-occupied, and the median age was 56.8.

Lakefront and forest property raises two items on the transfer return. The RETR asks for feet of water frontage, and it asks for acres in Managed Forest Law or Private Forest Crop programs. Owners of those programs must notify the Department of Natural Resources when ownership changes. For unpaid taxes, ask the Vilas County treasurer for a current statement before closing.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Vilas County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30 under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag). The seller also pays the state transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value, so a $150,000 sale carries a $450 fee, unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: What are the Vilas County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The office is open 8am to 4pm Monday through Friday and is closed on holidays. The recording cutoff is 3:00pm, and the e-recording cutoff is 2:45pm. The counter accepts cash or check only.

faqs.q: Who pays the Wisconsin transfer fee when a house sells?
faqs.a: The grantor, which is the seller, pays it. Wis. Stat. 77.22(1) imposes the fee on the grantor, and the register collects it when the deed is submitted for recording.

faqs.q: Do I pay a transfer fee when I inherit a house in Vilas County?
faqs.a: A transfer by will, descent or survivorship is exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11). The exemption number still has to appear on the deed or return, and the Register of Deeds forms list includes a Termination of Decedent's Property Interest.

faqs.q: What happens if a deed is never recorded?
faqs.a: An unrecorded conveyance is void against a later buyer who acts in good faith, pays value and records first, according to Wis. Stat. 706.08(1)(a). Record the deed promptly to protect the new owner.
